workflow-0073.pattern: Unchecked numeric values cross native boundaries without semantic or size validation

evidence.supports: An instrumented concurrent test suite intermittently hung because a worker subprocess could crash in a free-threaded build; the report attributed the resulting job hang to the crashed worker’s possibly wedged fault-reporting path and temporarily skipped the triggering test.

Fatal reporting in an instrumented free-threaded process ran without valid thread state and reached unsafe runtime traversal or non-progressing synchronization. The observed result was a hang or reporter failure instead of reliable termination.

workflow-0075.pattern: Concurrent asynchronous notifications reenter mutable callbacks without a nesting guard

workflow-0076.pattern: Unrestricted address discovery selects a protocol family unsupported by the runtime

evidence.supports: An allocation made for an alternate signal stack was later reported out of bounds during teardown. Reproductions across environments and persistence after increasing a fixed size multiplier support checking actual handler stack requirements rather than assuming a fixed heuristic is sufficient.

A dependency changed size-option conversion from integer-only behavior to screen-distance values. Tests and shared helpers required version-specific updates, supporting a stale dependency-contract expectation rather than an application memory-safety failure.

workflow-0087.pattern: Generated control flow retains unreachable operations after termination or configuration folding

workflow-0088.pattern: Parallel instrumented tests expose environment-sensitive subprocess failures

workflow-0094.pattern: Include-path ordering selects stale external configuration over the current generated header

workflow-0096.pattern: Independent compiler-capability checks redefine the same configuration symbol

workflow-0097.scope_note: This mixed cluster covers shutdown before residual activity is safely ordered or finished. Some members lose backing-state lifetime during cleanup; others use unlocked reads, incompatible atomic access, or incomplete barriers. Runtime, thread, and external-library state require different ownership and synchronization checks.

workflow-0100.scope_note: This umbrella covers unsynchronized shared-state access. Members differ: ordinary or partially atomic races lose state; replacement, resizing, or reinitialization invalidates borrowed state; cleanup races can release an allocation twice. A matching audit must identify the actual access, lifetime, or ownership mechanism rather than treating all races alike.

workflow-0120.pattern: Unnecessary tracking of immutable acyclic containers increases garbage-collection work

workflow-0127.pattern: Shutdown validation mistakes process-scoped blocked daemon workers for synchronously reclaimable threads

evidence.supports: Daemon server workers remained blocked in accept or request I/O when shutdown validation reported a thread leak. The report explains that a shutdown event does not cancel every blocking operation and that synchronous joining may hang; worker lifetime was intended to end with the process.

workflow-0132.pattern: Null string storage crosses a foreign-function boundary that requires a valid buffer

workflow-0135.pattern: Collector traversal reaches objects published before their fields are initialized

workflow-0140.scope_note: These reports concern deliberately altered low-level executable representations. Structural inconsistencies reach internal assertions, while incompatible metadata types reach invalid dereferences. This scope does not establish that all malformed executables can be validated or that ordinary construction exposes these failures.

workflow-0147.pattern: Ownership or representation invariants fail across managed-object boundaries
workflow-0147.scope_note: This mixed cluster includes ownership-accounting mismatches, premature release, stale freed storage, and deliberately corrupted live-object metadata. The common boundary is an unchecked lifetime or representation contract. Leaked ownership, stale access, and invalid object layout remain distinct mechanisms requiring different checks.

workflow-0158.pattern: Optimized runtime state remains usable after its assumptions require invalidation

workflow-0166.scope_note: The six reports involve metadata that does not match storage capacity or layout: native-width mismatches, invalid execution positions, undersized output buffers, underestimated producer sizes, and formatter suffix assumptions. They do not establish one buffer API or that every member causes actual memory damage.

workflow-0169.pattern: Toolchain and instrumentation combinations leave a generated-code target unusable during bootstrap

evidence.supports: Experimental generated code combined with undefined-behavior instrumentation failed during bootstrap on several compiler versions, with an invalid read in a lazy generated-code trampoline. The default compiler configuration succeeded, limiting the evidence to the reported configuration interaction.

workflow-0174.pattern: Native consumers trust extension-controlled results without validating their extent or shape

workflow-0179.pattern: Diagnostic metadata lookup uses an instruction representation outside the table index domain

workflow-0200.pattern: Lock-handoff assertions assume a held state that concurrent release can already change

workflow-0205.pattern: Uninstrumented dependency synchronization produces misleading sanitizer race reports

workflow-0206.pattern: Trace-size configuration exceeds generated-code metadata capacity

workflow-0210.scope_note: Initiating mechanisms include external metadata removal, incomplete copying, unresolved descriptors, and inconsistent tables. The common step is consuming absent or inconsistent metadata without validation. This does not establish leaked ownership or stale freed state; outcomes range from recoverable errors to assertions or invalid access.

workflow-0214.pattern: Truthiness dispatch omits a symbolic value category and reads an incompatible representation

workflow-0215.scope_note: This mixed cluster includes borrowed-state lifetime errors and externally invalidated mapped storage. The common step is using a view or destination without establishing its continued validity. Not every view must own its backing resource. The cause of the invalid destination in issue 140777 remains unresolved, so that member supports only the observed access failure.

evidence.supports: Manually prefixing an executable stream with a reserved metadata placeholder shifted its instructions and caused dispatch to abort on an internal invariant. The report identifies this as deliberately malformed low-level input outside ordinary supported construction.

A generated configuration probe consumed CPU without reaching its entry point. The stack was in instrumentation, allocator, loader, and system initialization, supporting a platform-dependent startup hang that leaves the synchronous configuration driver waiting.

workflow-0226.scope_note: This mixed cluster covers missing preconditions before representation access or arithmetic-sensitive operations. Members involve malformed typed values, assorted sanitizer-reported pointer and arithmetic cases, and timestamp range or clamping errors. Some collected findings still need individual investigation; the evidence does not establish one uniform failure mechanism.

evidence.supports: Noncanonical bytes copied into a native logical scalar reached typed access and triggered undefined-behavior diagnostics with platform-dependent results. The correction constrained portable paths and tests to valid representations.

Collected sanitizer findings involve absent storage, oversized positions, invalid logical representations, and extreme arithmetic inputs reaching operations without required preconditions. Some paths returned an expected value despite evaluating an invalid intermediate operation; individual findings require separate assessment.

Extreme timestamps exposed inconsistent range validation and later packing failures. Clamping could be bypassed by conversion overflow, and an upper clamp failed to round-trip precisely because it did not account for the target encoding granularity.

workflow-0233.pattern: Concurrent traversal uses runtime-owned records without stable references or teardown exclusion
workflow-0233.scope_note: Two mechanisms share an unstable traversal boundary: runtime-record teardown during diagnostic collection, and container mutation between borrowed-entry retrieval and ownership acquisition. Apply this pattern only where a traversal lacks the exclusion, snapshot, or lifetime protection required by the observed reference.

workflow-0239.pattern: A logically dead object remains collector-visible across interruptible destruction
